metadata.dataset_description: The dataset consists of 500 entries simulating ServiceNow fm_expense_line table, which records various attributes of financial expenses. Key fields include 'number', 'opened_at', 'amount', 'state', 'short_description', 'ci', 'user', 'department', 'category', 'process_date', 'source_id', and 'type'. This table documents the flow of financial transactions by detailing the amount, departmental allocation, and the nature of each expense. Provides a clear view of organizational expenditures across different categories, highlighting both the timing and the approval state of each financial entry.
metadata.goal: To identify and rectify the causes of high rejection rates in travel expenses to ensure that submissions  align with organizational policies.

predicted_insights: Although IT has the highest decline rate, Customer Support accounts for the majority of all declined Travel expenses—57% (35 of 61)—so focusing remediation on Customer Support submissions will likely yield the largest reduction in overall rejections.

The average monthly decline rate across this period was about 41.7%, peaking in Nov-2023 (57.1%) and Mar-2024 (53.8%) while dipping in Sep-2023 (21.4%) and Apr-2024 (27.3%); notably, Jan–Mar 2024 averaged ~49.2%, suggesting early-year travel submissions face elevated rejection risk and may need targeted policy reminders or pre-checks.

Rejections are not monotonic with amount—lower and mid amounts have the highest decline rates (Q1 48.6%, Q3 47.2%) while the highest amounts have the lowest (Q4 32.4%), a 16.2 percentage-point gap, indicating rejections are not driven by high-value claims alone.
About 2 out of every 5 Travel submissions lacking a source_id are declined (41.78%), highlighting source_id completeness as a high-impact lever to reduce rejections.

Lower-value travel claims are rejected about 50% more often than top-quartile claims (48.65% vs 32.43%), with a non-monotonic pattern and a notable mid-amount bump (Q3 at 47.22%), highlighting Q1 and Q3 as priority bands for reducing declines.
Across 61 declined Travel submissions, the top 6 users (led by Ofelia’s 4) account for 19 (≈31%), indicating that targeted guidance for a small cohort could materially reduce rejection rates.

Although IT has the highest decline rate, the majority of Travel declines come from Customer Support (35 of 61 total declines, ~57%), indicating that improving Customer Support submissions could yield the largest reduction in overall rejections.

Travel accounts for 146 of the dataset’s 172 records missing source_id (~85%), suggesting a category-specific process gap in capturing source references that likely contributes substantially to Travel expense rejections.
Nearly 42% of Travel submissions lacking a source_id are declined, suggesting that enforcing source_id completeness could materially reduce rejections within this subgroup.

Across the period, the average decline rate was about 41.7% (median 42.86%) with a wide range of 21.43–57.14 percentage points; the largest month-over-month swing was a 26.6 pp drop from Mar (53.85%) to Apr 2024 (27.27%), signaling abrupt process or compliance changes.

High-value travel claims show notable friction: declines equal processed outcomes (12 each) and 35.1% (13/37) remain unfinalized (Submitted+Pending), signaling greater uncertainty and potential policy misalignment at amounts ≥ 5,816.

Across 54 users, 24 (44%) exceeded a 40% Travel decline rate and together accounted for 45 declined claims; five users had every Travel submission declined (100%), and the median total submissions within this high-decline group was only 2.5, indicating many rejections stem from infrequent submitters even as a repeat filer (3 declines out of 7) signals policy/process confusion among frequent travelers too.
predicted_summary:
Travel expense declines are concentrated in a few departments: Customer Support accounts for 35 of 61 declines (57.4%) at a 44.3% decline rate (35/79), Sales contributes 18 declines (29.5%) at a 40.9% rate (18/44), and IT has the highest decline rate at 54.5% (6/11) but fewer cases; together, Customer Support and Sales drive 86.9% of all declines.
Missing source_id is pervasive and coincides with high rejection: all analyzed Travel submissions (146) lacked a source_id, with 61 declines (41.8% decline rate); no records with a source_id were available for comparison, indicating a widespread metadata gap within this category.
Declines are concentrated among a small set of users: six individuals—Ofelia Sheffler (4 declines), Cristina Sharper (3), Leif Bachta (3), Rob Woodbyrne (3), Sal Pindell (3), and Zackary Mockus (3)—account for 19 of 61 declines (31.1%) between Jun-2023 and Apr-2024, while many others show high decline rates on very small submission counts.
